question: Who wrote the novel "Life of Pi"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Yann Martel.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Yann Martel wrote the novel** "Life of Pi." **
 
• The novel was first published in **2001** and won the **Man Booker Prize **in the same year.
 
• **"Life of Pi"** is a work of fiction that tells the story of a young Indian boy named** Pi** who survives a shipwreck and spends** 227 days** adrift in the **Pacific Ocean **on a lifeboat with a **Bengal tiger**.
 
• The novel explores themes of **spirituality, religion, and the human condition.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jonathan Safran Foer** is an American author known for his novels **"Everything Is Illuminated"** and** "Extremely Loud and Incredibly Close."**
 
• **Khaled Hosseini **is an Afghan-American author known for his novels **"The Kite Runner," "A Thousand Splendid Suns," and "And the Mountains Echoed."**
 
• **Carol Birch **is a British author known for her novels **"Jamrach's Menagerie" and "Orphans of the Carnival."**
